data.title: Joby Stock Tumbles Today: What Spooked Investors and What Wall Street Sees Next
data.description:
Joby Aviation (NYSE:JOBY) stock is sinking about 7% on Friday after Barclays downgraded the electric air taxi developer from Equal Weight to Underweight (equivalent to Sell) and slashed its price target from $6 to $4. The downgrade reflects concerns that the company's strategy of manufacturing, operating, and servicing its own aircraft could prove too costly, even if it becomes the first competitor to secure regulatory certification.

Barclays analyst Anthony Valentini believes investors are placing too much value on Joby's potential first-mover advantage, arguing that an early lead may not translate into market dominance. The analyst also doubts whether the company's aircraft can accommodate enough passengers to serve the broader market or whether its production capacity can support substantial growth.

"We don't see the EVTOL market as winner takes all," Valentini warns, suggesting that competitors could still capture significant opportunities even if Joby reaches certification first.

Promotion

High conviction JOBY bulls now have this Tradr ETF

The analyst is particularly concerned about the company's decision to handle nearly every aspect of its operations internally. While this approach could eventually allow Joby to capture more revenue, it also requires substantial spending before passenger flights begin generating income. Valentini believes selling aircraft directly to customers would provide faster returns and potentially better profitability than collecting revenue one passenger at a time.

"We view this strategy as too aggressive and too capital and time intensive," the analyst explains, adding that Joby's strong financial position and potential certification lead do not justify its premium valuation.

The downgrade comes during a difficult year for Joby, whose shares have lost more than half their value since the beginning of 2026. Nevertheless, the company continues preparing for commercial air taxi operations, leaving investors to weigh its technological progress against the substantial costs of bringing its aircraft to market.

Adding to those concerns, a Florida federal jury recently awarded aircraft component manufacturer Aerosonic nearly $116.9 million in a trade secrets dispute involving Joby Aero. The jury found that the developer violated a confidentiality agreement and misappropriated technology related to aircraft sensors, creating another potential financial burden as the company invests heavily in certification and production.

Joby has also encountered legal difficulties in its ongoing dispute with rival Archer Aviation. In late September, a California federal court dismissed several claims from Joby's lawsuit against Archer, along with Archer's counterclaims, although other portions of the case remain unresolved. The two competitors continue pursuing commercial air taxi operations, with their respective certification timelines likely to influence investor confidence.

Despite these setbacks, some investors remain optimistic about the industry's longer-term prospects. Cathie Wood's ARK funds have continued purchasing shares of both Joby and Archer, suggesting that Wood still sees opportunities in electric aviation despite the considerable obstacles facing these companies.

Barclays may be betting against Joby, but the broader Wall Street picture is less one-sided. Among the 8 analysts covering JOBY, 2 recommend Buy, 3 suggest Hold, and another 3 advise Sell, giving the stock a Hold (i.e., Neutral) consensus rating. Yet, the average 12-month price target of $10.56 implies about 97% upside from current levels. (See JOBY stock forecast)

data.title: Why Are Gold and Silver Up Today, 10/9/26?
data.description:
Both gold (XAUUSD) and silver (XAGUSD) are in the green on Friday with gains of 1.51% and 2.55%, respectively. The gains come as interest rate hike expectations at the October 28 Fed meeting remain subdued. The odds of a 25-basis-point hike are at 19.4%, slightly up from 17.7% a day ago, according to the CME FedWatch tool.

Higher rates are generally viewed as a negative for the two precious metals, as they don't generate interest. When rates rise, the opportunity cost of holding gold and silver compared to interest-bearing assets, such as Treasury bonds, increases.

Inflation Reports Could Drive Gold and Silver Volatility

Gold and silver could face volatility next week, as investors will receive two major inflation updates. Higher-than-expected readings could raise rate hike odds and weigh on the precious metals. On Wednesday, the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) will publish the latest Consumer Price Index (CPI) update, followed by the Producer Price Index (PPI) on Thursday.

data.title: Intel Stock (NASDAQ:INTC) Slips Despite Chance of New DDR4 Processors Next Year
data.description:
Those hoping that today's news would turn chip stock Intel (INTC) around were sadly disappointed. But, those hoping for new DDR4 processors out of Intel will be much less disappointed if a new report from TechPowerUp goes through. A new set of BIOS updates from GIGABYTE were released recently that puts the entire motherboard for Intel B760 and H610 units in line to receive LGA1700 processors. Those processors are expected to launch sometime in early 2027. This news did not help things much with investors as they sent Intel shares down modestly in Friday afternoon's trading. Intel has seen a 199.26% rally in its share price over the past year.

A Simple Update

Once these motherboards go live, owners will only need to flash new firmware and then add the new CPU once it actually shows up, as the update covers both DDR4 and DDR5 boards, noted the report. This actually meshes with an earlier report suggesting that the LGA1700 chips would be ready in 2027 because they are built around the original Raptor Lake silicon. So if that report ultimately tracks, then the motherboards necessary should be ready about the same time.

Essentially the revelation of GIGABYTE's BIOS update is the closest thing that we have had yet to a confirmation of the new DDR4 processors, as Intel has not actually announced them yet. Further, the report notes no release of Z790, Z690, or B660 boards. These may simply be coming later, or they may not be coming at all, limiting customers to certain options.

A "Show Me" Year Ahead

2026 was a year of recovery for Intel, noted a report from The Motley Fool. But 2027 will likely require Intel to demonstrate that it is worth its expanded value. Certainly Intel's product line is solid as it is. It still remains the leader in the CPU space even if that lead has been chipped away substantially by its various competitors. And with its foundry ambitions starting to run at their fullest peak, there is a good chance that Intel will have plenty of high-volume customers in the near-term future.

But good chances do not necessarily make for good revenue streams. So many will be watching Intel closely in the near-term future to see if any of the possibilities turn into actual orders. With Wall Street projections looking for only 15% revenue growth next year, Intel stock is likely to lose a large portion of the gains that it achieved this year.

data.title: Apple Stock (AAPL) Could Gain $75 per Share from AI, Dan Ives Says
data.description:
Tech giant Apple (AAPL) could gain roughly $75 in value per share from artificial intelligence, according to Yorkville Ives analyst Dan Ives, who has a $400 price target on the stock. Ives believes that Apple can become a major winner in AI without developing the most powerful models itself. Instead, its advantage comes from controlling access to more than 2.5 billion active devices, including 1.5 billion iPhones. He expects that this position could help Apple generate more services revenue while encouraging customers to upgrade their devices.

In a note to clients, Ives described Apple as "the toll collector on the consumer AI highway." The comparison describes how Apple already makes money through its App Store, even though outside developers create many of the apps that customers use. AI could work in a similar way.

Rather than spending billions to develop every advanced model itself, Apple could make AI services available through its existing devices. That would give other AI companies access to Apple's enormous customer base while creating opportunities for Apple to collect additional revenue.

AI Could Boost Apple's Services Revenue and iPhone Sales

More specifically, Ives estimates that AI-related products could eventually account for more than 15% of Apple's Services revenue. That business already generates income from subscriptions and App Store purchases, so additional AI features could provide another source of growth.

Apple's recent financial performance provides some context. The company reported $109.4 billion in revenue during its June quarter, an increase of 16% from the previous year. Services revenue also reached a June-quarter record.

Meanwhile, Ives believes that AI could help drive another wave of iPhone upgrades. He estimates that approximately 375 million iPhones have not been replaced in more than four years. More useful AI features could encourage those customers to purchase newer models.

The analyst is also optimistic about Apple's new foldable iPhone Duo. He expects approximately 10 million sales over the next few quarters, with a best-case scenario of 15 million units through the holiday season. However, Nikkei Asia reported on Friday that Apple has reduced October component orders for its iPhone 18 Pro models by at least 15% following weaker demand.

data.title: Moderna Stock (MRNA) Climbs 13% to Top Its 52-Week High — Here's Why
data.description:
Moderna shares (MRNA) climbed by 13% to around $223 on Friday afternoon, pushing the U.S. biotech and pharma company past its one-year high of $212.22. The rally came as the vaccine maker replaced entertainment company Warner Bros. on the Nasdaq 100 index before the market open today, October 9. Warner Bros. is now part of a new media powerhouse, Skydance Corporation (SKYD). It merged with Paramount Skydance in a $110 billion takeover completed on Tuesday.

For context, the Nasdaq 100 is a flagship U.S. index that tracks the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq stock exchange. Inclusion in the benchmark means exchange-traded funds that track the index must include MRNA stock in their portfolios. This is bullish for demand for Moderna's shares.

data.title: Palantir Stock Extends Rally Today: Why This Investor Sounds the Alarm
data.description:
Palantir (NASDAQ:PLTR) stock is climbing nearly 4% on Friday, extending its rally to 64% since the company's August 3 earnings report. Today's gains come as Wall Street grows more optimistic about the software giant, with Barclays initiating coverage on PLTR with an Overweight rating (equivalent to Buy) and a $265 price target, implying about 29% upside from current levels.

Investors have good reasons to feel optimistic about Palantir's prospects, particularly following its stellar second-quarter results. Revenue surged 93% year-over-year, while U.S. commercial sales jumped 149%, demonstrating the company's growing presence in the AI market.

However, while the numbers continue to excite the market, investor Paul Franke, who has spent 40 years researching financial markets, is sounding the alarm, warning that Palantir's sky-high valuation could leave investors facing devastating losses.

Promotion

"My issue is paying greater than 50x EPS several years into the future is quite risky with intermediate 'risk-free' Treasury bonds in the 4.5% to 5% range today," Franke explains.

His concerns become clearer when comparing Palantir with other tech companies competing in the AI market. PLTR trades at around 55 times estimated 2026 revenue, compared with a median multiple of just five times among the peers he examined. Furthermore, analysts expect earnings expansion to moderate during 2027 and 2028, potentially making today's elevated pricing harder to justify.

Another concern involves insider selling, which Franke believes deserves closer scrutiny given the stock's recent performance. Executives have consistently reduced their holdings since the summer, although such transactions do not necessarily indicate concerns about future performance.

Looking ahead, Franke expects Palantir shares to trade between $140 and $210 over the next 12 months, while acknowledging that a move toward $250 remains possible. However, his outlook becomes much more pessimistic if enthusiasm for AI weakens or the broader market enters a prolonged downturn.

"My opinion: eclipsing the $106 low in June will not be difficult in any future AI bust," Franke warns. The investor argues that the possibility of a 25% gain does not justify risking a loss of as much as 50% over the coming year.

Ultimately, Franke assigns PLTR a Sell rating and has a small short position as protection against his other tech investments. (To watch Franke's track record, click here)

Wall Street may be more optimistic about Palantir than Franke, but its price targets tell a less encouraging story. The average 12-month forecast of $208.29 implies a mere 1.17% upside from current levels. Yet, of the 24 analysts covering PLTR, 19 recommend Buy, three assign Hold ratings, and only 2 advise Sell, giving the stock a Moderate Buy consensus. (See PLTR stock forecast)

data.title: Boeing Makes List of Buys for the Modern-Day Industrial Revolution—Boeing Stock (NYSE:BA) Gains
data.description:
Have you ever considered what a modern-day industrial revolution might look like? Aerospace stock Boeing (BA) actually figures into it, based on a report from Barron's, that notes Boeing landed a slot in a list of buys for the modern-day industrial revolution. Investors found this news welcome enough, and gave Boeing a modest boost in Friday afternoon's trading. Boeing has seen a 10.9% loss in its share price over the past year.

It Has Nothing to Do With Steampunk

The Barron's report noted that Barclays analyst Anthony Valentini launched coverage of 20 different aerospace and defense stocks. Boeing, not surprisingly, made it onto that list with a Buy rating and a price target of $300 per share.

Defense stocks have been weak lately, mostly as investors start getting concerned about contract reform at the Pentagon and the midterm elections. If the midterm elections swing toward the Democrats, as some believe they might, then there could be some spending gridlock issues as the president looks for one thing to happen and Congress looks for completely different things. Boeing's positions in space travel, the defense industry, and commercial aircraft all make it a worthwhile pick as far as somebody who's looking for a modern-day industrial revolution is concerned.

Meanwhile, Southwest Airlines (LUV) is apparently looking to buy Boeing 787s to start taking on long-haul international flights, according to a report from Live and Let's Fly. But that same report suggests that Southwest might actually be better off by using the planes it already has, but with a minor design change: adding lie-flat beds to the cabin spaces.

Naturally, Southwest hasn't made any decisions yet on this. But the report suggests that Southwest may be interested in a fleet of aircraft measuring in the dozens. Earlier reports suggest that Southwest may add anywhere from eight to 12 long-haul destinations in order to cover the bulk of locations that Southwest travelers want to go to. Whether or not Boeing will be a part of those plans is anybody's guess right now. But with many common European destinations running between 2,850 and 3,450 nautical miles, these should be well within reach for a 737 MAX 8, which has a range of around 3,550 nautical miles.

data.title: Aura Minerals Stock (AUGO) Soars Over 11% on a Q3 Mining Update
data.description:
Aura Minerals (AUGO) stock soared on Friday after the mining company provided investors with a business update. A press release from the company highlighted that it hit a new production record in the third quarter of 2026.

The gold miner produced 95,557 gold equivalent ounces (GEO), up 27% from the prior quarter and 29% from the same period last year. Sales reached 93,742 GEO, a 20% rise from the second quarter. For the first nine months of 2026, output totaled 253,131 GEO at current prices, up 28% year over year and the highest level for that period in the company's history.

Borborema and MSG led the gains. Borborema produced 22,842 GEO, a quarterly record and a 60% jump from the prior quarter. Higher ore grades and better plant feed drove the rise. At MSG, output climbed 85% to 13,321 GEO as work to restore the mine moved ahead. Aranzazu also had a strong quarter, with output up 39% from Q2 to 24,920 GEO.

  • Apoena raised output 20% from the prior quarter to 6,865 GEO as work at its Nosde pit reached key high-grade areas.
  • Minosa output fell 7% to 13,344 GEO due to lower ore feed and the effects of a prior rise in leach-pad stacking levels.
  • Almas output dropped 12% to 14,264 GEO as lower grades offset gains from its plant upgrade. The company expects higher-grade ore to help Almas in the fourth quarter.

CEO Rodrigo Barbosa said Aura Minerals remained on track to meet its full-year targets, with further growth expected in Q4. The company also noted that work at its Era Dorada project remained on time and on budget, with overall physical progress at 13.1%. Aura Minerals plans to keep advancing its mine upgrades and the MSG turnaround as it works to lift output in the final quarter.

data.title: AST SpaceMobile CEO Touts Spectrum 'No One Can Match' as ASTS Stock Sinks 15% on SpaceX Threat
data.description:
Shares in AST SpaceMobile (ASTS), the satellite-based cellular network builder, plunged by 15% to about $49 on Friday afternoon, extending the previous day's 6.13% fall. This followed an industry-wide sell-off after aerospace and rocket giant SpaceX (SPCX) confirmed it had agreed to buy 800 MHz of low-band spectrum from private investment firm Grain Management. Reports estimate the deal at $8 billion, with the move seen as a potential threat to traditional network providers. Reacting, Abel Avellan, AST's chair and CEO, boasted in an X post that the company can deploy "critical low-band and mid-band spectrum that no one can match!"

Why ASTS Stock Is Plunging on SpaceX's $8B Spectrum Push

For context, low-band spectrum is radio frequency "lanes" that can travel farther and penetrate buildings. Mid-band spectrum, meanwhile, travels far less but carries more data.

Investors appear to think acquiring the spectrum portfolio could help SpaceX's Starlink compete directly with the country's largest carriers, AT&T (T), Verizon (VZ), and T-Mobile U.S. (TMUS) in metropolitan areas. This could be achieved through a hybrid terrestrial infrastructure.

Promotion

ASTX: an alternative to margin or options on ASTS

In addition, as Starlink already offers a well-established satellite network targeting rural areas, investors also seem to think this ground-and-space expansion could give SpaceX a decisive advantage over AST. Notably, AST relies on partnerships with those same legacy carriers.

AST Defends Advantage Amid SpaceX Threat

In the X post, Avellan noted that its U.S. mobile carrier partners have about 1,000 MHz of low- and mid-band spectrum that his company's satellite network can use. He also pointed to the company's own portfolio of 45 MHz of L-band spectrum.

This spectrum also travels relatively far. It can also handle obstacles such as weather, trees, and buildings better than higher-frequency bands.

"With our current satellites in orbit and in build, our United States partners will access critical low-band and mid-band spectrum that no one can match!" Avellan wrote.

He continued, "When combined with the mobile network operators' extensive spectrum assets, and in combination with AST SpaceMobile-controlled 45 MHz of L-band spectrum, users will see peak data rates of nearly 200 Mbps from the largest-ever satellites in low Earth orbit."

Is AST SpaceMobile Stock a Good Buy or Sell?

On Wall Street, AST SpaceMobile's shares remain a Moderate Buy based on analysts' consensus ratings. This breaks down into five Buys and six Holds issued by 11 analysts over the past three months.

However, the average ASTS price target of $86.42 suggests about 77% upside ahead (see ASTS stock forecast here).
